liebermann.notes: Holkham 228, owned by Archbishop Matthew Parker and then Edward Coke. Prefixed late-16th-c. leaves (Quadr. Arg., related to Dm); the main part, written c. 1200, is the latest recension of Quadripartitus (class m) with the Latin laws from I–II Cnut through Alfred–Ine, Athelstan, Edgar, Æthelred, Edward, Edmund, Rect, CHn cor, Quadr. II, De archidiaconibus, Hn com, then Pseudo-Ulpianus De edendo. Later additions: ff. 117–40 (c. 1570, from C: IV Eg Lat, Epistola Eleutherii from the London interpolation of ECf, ECf retr rubrics), ff. 141–57 (c. 1230: Leis Wl and Cons Cn incomplete, ECf); the rest c. 1600.

wormald.wormald_date: s. xii^3/4 (p. 237); placed before T, following Gullick and Liebermann (p. 238 n. 305)
wormald.wormald_origin: Origin and provenance unknown until owned by Archbishop Parker, then Sir Edward Coke and his descendants at Holkham Hall (p. 237); Parkerian copy of the 'Argumentum' 'e libro veteri ecclesiae Wigorniensis' inserted at front (p. 239 n. 312); large parts copied by Nowell in University of California MS 170/529 (p. 238 n. 305)

wormald.other_contents: Smallest of the set; supplemented by other legal texts; extensive additions by Parker's circle; Ine rubrics moved to front of code, full rubrication (pp. 238, 242).
wormald.overview: A small copy of the final Quadripartitus recension from the third quarter of the twelfth century, matching M in content and order, to which other scribes later added further legal texts. It belonged to Archbishop Parker, whose circle added to it extensively, and then to Sir Edward Coke, whose descendants kept it at Holkham Hall; it is now in the British Library. Wormald treats Coke's ownership as a sign of how long this Latin collection went on being used.
wormald.key_quote: It is more than symbolically significant that one of the surviving copies belonged to Sir Edward Coke (p. 244)
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: the guide gives 'Holkham Hall (Earl of Leicester), MS 228'; Wormald gives the current shelfmark BL, Additional MS 49366. Note the n. 305 wording 'following ... Liebermann himself in placing Hk before T' – so Liebermann's relative order agrees, though the guide's date c. 1200 vs T c. 1225 is later than Wormald's. GUIDE: Liebermann dates the main part c. 1200; Wormald s. xii³ᐟ⁴ (p. 237) — a modest difference (moved here from liebermann_superseded, since Wormald follows Liebermann's relative order, n. 305).
verify_notes: Checked p. 237 (image: s. xii³ᐟ⁴ confirmed), 238–9, 242–4, Table 4.7 (image): laws list matches.
liebermann_superseded removed (date c. 1200 vs s. xii³ᐟ⁴ not a striking correction, and Wormald explicitly follows Liebermann in placing Hk before T, n. 305); noted in doubts.
